prompt: A Ferris wheel car starts at the right side of the wheel and rotates $400^\circ$. What is the smallest positive angle that would have left it in exactly the same spot? Give just the number of degrees.
hint: One full trip around the wheel is $360^\circ$ — that much rotation puts you right back where you started.

hints.text: One full trip around the wheel is $360^\circ$ — that much rotation puts you right back where you started.
Peel off one full turn: compute $400^\circ - 360^\circ$.
$400^\circ - 360^\circ = 40^\circ$, so the car ends up $40^\circ$ around the wheel.

explanation: A full rotation is $360^\circ$, and rotating a full turn changes nothing about where you end up.
So subtract one full turn from $400^\circ$: $400^\circ - 360^\circ = 40^\circ$.
Angles that land in the same place are called coterminal, so $400^\circ$ and $40^\circ$ are coterminal.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think of it as an odometer
steps: Rotation is like a trip counter that resets every $360^\circ$.
Going $400^\circ$ is one complete lap plus $40^\circ$ of a second lap.
The lap does not show, so all you see is the extra $40^\circ$.
